title: upgrade attention kernels: FlashAttentionV2 + fused-ops + rope/rotary + KV-batching + scheduler
author: Ethan Walker
description: Motivation: reduce per-token cost and tail latency for long-context models by upgrading our attention execution path to FlashAttentionV2 and adding fused rotary/rope ops, plus tighter KV-batching and scheduler-driven routing. This PR introduces FlashAttentionV2 kernels with optional fused QKV+attention steps, a fused rope/rotary operator that avoids expensive elementwise kernels for long sequences, and KV-batching-aware scheduling heuristics to keep GPU utilization high without violating latency SLOs. Backwards compatibility: the new kernels are opt-in via runtime config and fall back to our previous aten path for unsupported CUDA/toolkit combos. Benchmarks: internal perf-canary shows 1.5-2.3x throughput on sequence lengths >2048 and 15-25% median p95 latency improvement for mixed request workloads in Dedicated. This PR also includes unit tests, integration tests for the continuous-batching path, updated canary configs, and documentation notes for model owners. Checklist: - Implement FlashAttentionV2 integration and wrappers; - Add fused rope/rotary kernel and tests; - Update KV batcher to expose batch-aware grouping keys and max-token heuristics; - Add scheduler policy to prioritize low-latency small requests while filling throughput windows; - Perf canary config and benchmark harness updates; - Docs and release notes. Runtime flag: runtime.features.use_flashattention_v2 (default false in this change; will be enabled in canary). Related: ENG-3489 (attention kernel upgrades), ENG-3612 (scheduling + KV batching).
